definition: A short code (e.g. L23, RPL4, SAFA1) identifying one specific field in one output file's record layout - the alphabetic prefix names the file (or, for SAF, the record type), the digits identify the field within it.
A fixed-width text file format (Geosupport's native input shape): one row per record, each field occupying fixed byte positions - see the Field Formatting section for the justify/fill conventions.
A street's borough digit plus its 5-digit street code (6 characters total) - identifies one specific name for a street within the city.
A B5SC plus a 2-digit LGC (8 characters total). A street can have more than one valid name (an LGC each), so this - not the B5SC alone - is what actually pins down one specific name variant.

Flags a field or output whose value depends on geometry - a spatial join (containment, intersection, proximity) or a geometric computation (ordering by position, clipping) - rather than an ordinary attribute/key join. Worth knowing at a glance: precision, boundary/overlap edge cases, and coordinate-system issues can all affect a geospatially determined value in ways a plain join never would.
A 2-digit code distinguishing one of a street's possibly-several official names (a street can have up to 4, in fields LGC1-4). Appended to a B5SC to form a B7SC.

On a divided street, the street is represented by two parallel roadbed segments (one per direction) plus one generic segment standing for the street as a whole. Some outputs report roadbed-specific data; others roll up to the generic segment - see the Roadbed Pointer List section for the mechanism connecting them.
One of the two directional segments making up a divided street - see generic_segment for how it relates to the street as a whole.
9 output files (see the Special Address File section) covering 13 CSCL address/place-name/intersection record types, each pertaining to a specific segment or node.
Named street intersections, keyed by NODEID rather than a segment - see Intersection.txt.
A Duplicate Address Pseudo-Street (DAPS): an alternate address range for a street that's also known by a different "regular" name elsewhere in the city - see GenericD.txt / RoadbedD.txt.
An address point tied to a specific physical segment - see GenericS.txt / RoadbedS.txt.
A vanity address: a building's alternate/promotional address on a street different from the one it physically sits on - see GenericOV.txt / RoadbedOV.txt.
